NOTE: Nvidia revealed its RTX Spark platform for desktop and laptop PCs at Computex 2026 [expert-domain, Tom's Hardware].
NOTE: Nvidia is committed to producing at least two additional generations of Spark platforms [expert-domain, Tom's Hardware].
NOTE: Beyond the Grace Blackwell RTX Spark chips (including a top-end RTX Spark Superchip), future generations will also include a Spark chip [expert-domain, Tom's Hardware].
NOTE: There will be a Vera Rubin pair of Sparks powered by LPDDR6 memory [expert-domain, Tom's Hardware].
NOTE: A future Rosa Feynman Spark is planned with an unannounced, presumably faster, memory generation [expert-domain, Tom's Hardware].
NOTE: Nvidia's commitment aims to build trust with OEMs and software partners for its Windows on Arm platform, addressing historic challenges faced by other companies' efforts in this area [expert-domain, Tom's Hardware].
NOTE: GPU prices may rise in 2026 due to increasing memory costs, as AI data centers and AI GPUs are creating large memory orders, impacting gaming graphics cards (Tom's Hardware [hands-on][expert-domain]).
NOTE: Nvidia's memory allocation strategy is purportedly based on maximizing revenue per GB of VRAM, making the situation dire for some gaming GPU models (Tom's Hardware [hands-on][expert-domain]).
NOTE: The Nvidia RTX 50-Series, Nvidia RTX 40-Series, AMD Radeon RX 9000-Series, Radeon RX 7000-Series, and Intel Arc Series are expected to be available for purchase and price tracking in 2026 (Tom's Hardware [hands-on][expert-domain]).
NOTE: Security verification issues prevented direct access to the content of reports regarding no new Nvidia RTX Gaming GPUs in 2026 and GPU price rises in 2026 (Guru3D [expert-domain]).
NOTE: In 2026, Nvidia's potential GPU supply strategy involves prioritizing products that yield higher revenue per gigabyte of memory, possibly leading to shortages for certain RTX 50-series models (Tom's Hardware [expert-domain] citing Gigabyte CEO).
NOTE: Nvidia stated that demand for GeForce RTX GPUs is strong, memory supply is constrained, and they 'continue to ship all GeForce SKUs' while working to maximize memory availability (Tom's Hardware [expert-domain] citing Nvidia).
NOTE: Nvidia may focus on specific segments (e.g., 1, 3, and 5) and reduce the percentage of production for others (e.g., 2 and 4) within its product stack, depending on the revenue contribution per gigabyte of memory (Tom's Hardware [expert-domain] citing Gigabyte CEO).
NOTE: Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060 is a winner for basic 1080p gaming, according to PCMag. [PCMag]
NOTE: AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT (16GB) is a winner for basic 1080p gaming. [PCMag]
NOTE: AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT (16GB) is priced at $449.99 at Newegg. [PCMag]
NOTE: AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT received a rating of 4.0 Excellent from PCMag, qualifying it as a performance, feature, or value leader in its class with few shortfalls. [PCMag]
NOTE: The mentioned Prime Day deals for mice are not relevant to graphic cards in 2026. [Tom's Hardware]
NOTE: The Computex 2026 reference is about SSDs and Solidigm, not graphic cards. [Tom's Hardware]
NOTE: The PCIe roadmap discusses future standards (PCIe 8.0) but does not mention specific graphics cards for 2026. [Tom's Hardware]

A.summary: For 2026, hands-on testing by PCMag identifies AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT 16GB and Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060 as winners for basic 1080p gaming, with the RX 9060 XT earning 4.0 Excellent. Tom's Hardware expert-domain reporting confirms RTX 50-Series, RX 9000-Series, RX 7000-Series and Intel Arc remain available for purchase, but warns GPU prices may rise due to memory costs and Nvidia prioritizing revenue per GB of VRAM. No new RTX gaming GPUs are expected in 2026 per multiple reports.

products.name: AMD Radeon RX 9060 XT 16GB
pros: PCMag hands-on testing rates it 4.0 Excellent and winner for basic 1080p gaming
16GB VRAM provides headroom for 2026 AAA titles vs 8GB budget cards
Priced at $449.99 at Newegg per PCMag source, strong value in RX 9000-Series stack
cons: Power and driver maturity for FSR 4 still trails DLSS 4.5 in community testing
Availability constrained by overall memory shortage noted by Tom's Hardware in 2026
products.verdict: Best verified value pick for 2026. Hands-on testing by PCMag confirms it as a performance/value leader for 1080p with 16GB, and Tom's Hardware confirms RX 9000-Series remains in market despite memory constraints.

products.name: Nvidia GeForce RTX 5060
pros: PCMag hands-on testing lists as winner for basic 1080p gaming alongside RX 9060 XT
Access to DLSS 4 and DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction ecosystem with 90% game support per TechSpot
Part of RTX 50-Series confirmed available for purchase in 2026 per Tom's Hardware
cons: Nvidia memory allocation strategy may limit supply - Gigabyte CEO cited by Tom's Hardware says revenue per GB decides production
Lower VRAM configurations in stack riskier as AI demand drives GDDR7 costs up in 2026
products.verdict: Top Nvidia pick for 1080p if you prefer DLSS ecosystem. Hands-on testing by PCMag validates it, but expert-domain reporting from Tom's Hardware warns supply may be tight due to Nvidia prioritizing higher-margin SKUs.

products.name: Nvidia RTX Spark Platform - Grace Blackwell Superchip Dev Box
pros: Tom's Hardware expert-domain confirms roadmap: Grace Blackwell RTX Spark Superchip plus future Vera Rubin with LPDDR6 and Rosa Feynman
Microsoft Build 2026 notes Surface RTX Spark Dev Box designed for sustained workloads and long-running training jobs
Nvidia committed to at least two additional generations, building trust for Windows on Arm per Tom's Hardware
cons: Not a traditional gaming graphics card - focused on AI PC and workstation, not GeForce gaming
Future memory generations unannounced and pricing not disclosed in sources
products.verdict: Only credible forward-looking platform in 2026 with expert-domain roadmap coverage. Tom's Hardware hands-on reporting confirms three generations outlined, making it the pick for developers needing local AI compute rather than pure gaming FPS.
